mainTopic: מוקצה of broken and leftover items on שבת, the מחלוקת about old oven shards, and a new משנה about a stone in a water gourd
overview: This amud finishes a ruling about a broken jug seal (מגופה): if it was thrown in the garbage before שבת, it becomes מוקצה. It then asks whether leftover pieces of objects may be moved on שבת. The basic test is whether the pieces are still good for some use. Mat shreds are permitted because they can cover filth, just as the mat covers dirt. Tiny cloak rags smaller than three by three are forbidden, because nobody uses them. Pieces of an old oven are a מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה. אביי, רבא, and רב אשי each explain the root of that argument; in the end, רב אשי says it is about shards used as a baking tile (טפקא). רבינא shows that the custom of moving oven covers without handles follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. Finally, a new משנה begins about a stone inside a water gourd: the gourd may be used on שבת only if the stone does not fall out.

steps.title: A seal thrown in the garbage before שבת is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The closing clause of the ברייתא about a broken jug seal: if the owner threw it into the garbage before שבת, it may not be moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he threw it into the garbage dump while it was still day, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a ברייתא from the previous discussion about the clay seal of a jug (מגופה). If the owner threw the seal into the garbage before שבת began, it may not be moved on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a broken seal may be moved, because it can still be used. But throwing it into the trash before שבת shows that the owner gave up on it. So it becomes מוקצה. What decides the law here is the owner's own action, not the item itself.

keyTerms.meaning: While it was still day (before שבת began)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the theme of the whole passage: whether a person still treats an item as usable decides whether it is מוקצה.

phrases.english: If he threw it into the garbage dump while it was still day —
phrases.notes: "It" refers to the clay jug seal from the ברייתא.

phrases.english: it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: Forbidden to move on שבת, because he showed he gave up on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the ברייתא about the jug seal begun on the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A seal thrown into the garbage before שבת becomes מוקצה.

steps.title: Shreds of a mat may be moved on שבת
steps.stepSummary: שמואל, quoted by בר המדורי, rules that reed shreds that came off a mat may be moved on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר המדורי said in the name of שמואל: the shreds of a mat may be moved on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling begins. שמואל says that loose reed pieces that came off a mat are not מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think these shreds are just junk. שמואל says they still count as usable objects. The reason is not given yet. The גמרא will ask for it next.

keyTerms.meaning: It is permitted to move them

phrases.english: Bar Hamduri said that Shmuel said:
Shreds of a mat —
phrases.notes: Reed pieces that came apart from the mat.

phrases.english: it is permitted to move them on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case in the same topic: leftover pieces of objects on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mat shreds are not מוקצה and may be moved.

steps.title: Why are mat shreds permitted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind שמואל's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the shreds are allowed. This question sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Small shreds look useless, so the leniency needs a reason. The question asks what use makes them count as a כלי.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What use makes mat shreds still count as usable?

steps.title: The shreds do the same job as the mat
steps.stepSummary: רבא reports what בר המדורי told him: a mat is used to cover dirt, and the shreds can also cover filth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: בר המדורי explained it to me. What is the mat itself good for? For covering dirt. These shreds are also good for covering filth.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the reason, which he heard directly from בר המדורי. The shreds are permitted because they can still do the mat's basic job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mat was never a fancy item. It was used to cover dirt on the ground. A shred can still cover a small dirty spot. Since its use is the same kind of use as the original, it keeps its status as a usable item.
steps.whatToRemember: A leftover piece is not מוקצה if it can still do the same kind of job the whole item did.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא, בַּר הַמְדּוּרֵי אַסְבְּרַהּ לִי:
phrases.english: Rava said: Bar Hamduri explained it to me:
The mat itself, what is it good for?
To cover dirt with it.
These shreds are also fit
phrases.notes: Fit for the same kind of use.

phrases.english: to cover filth with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, בַּר הַמְדּוּרֵי אַסְבְּרַהּ לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The shreds can still cover filth, just as the mat covers dirt.

steps.title: Leftover pieces of cloaks may not be moved
steps.stepSummary: רב, quoted by רבי זירא, rules that the remnants of cloaks are forbidden to move on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רב: remnants of cloaks may not be moved on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ruling: leftover scraps from cloaks are מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Compare this with the mat shreds, which were permitted. Here the leftovers are forbidden. This raises a question: cloth scraps are often usable, so why are these forbidden? אביי will explain in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It is forbidden to move them

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rav said:
Remnants of cloaks —
it is forbidden to move them on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A contrasting case: these leftovers are forbidden, while the mat shreds were permitted.

steps.title: אביי limits the ruling to tiny rags
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that רב means only rags smaller than three by three fingerbreadths, which neither poor nor rich people would use.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: this is talking about rags that are less than three by three, which are not useful to poor people or to rich people.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי narrows רב's ruling. Only very small scraps are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rag of three by three fingerbreadths or more is still useful, at least to a poor person, so it may be moved. A smaller scrap is useless to everyone, so it is מוקצה. The test is the same one used for the mat: is it still usable?
steps.confusionAlert: רב did not forbid all cloth scraps. Only scraps that are too small for anyone to use are forbidden.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּמַטְלָנִיּוֹת שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶן שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ,
phrases.english: This is about rags that are not three by three,
which are not fit for poor people
and not for rich people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines exactly which case רב's ruling in step 5 covers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only scraps smaller than three by three, useless to everyone, are forbidden.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: pieces of an old oven may be moved
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records רבי מאיר's view that pieces of an old oven may be moved in a courtyard, like any other כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן taught: pieces of an old oven are like all other כלים that may be moved in a courtyard. This is the view of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a new case. רבי מאיר treats the pieces of a broken old oven as ordinary movable כלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An oven was fixed in place and was not moved around. Even so, רבי מאיר holds that once it breaks, its pieces can be used for something, such as covering or supporting things. So they are like any other כלי.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Pieces of an old oven
are like all the vessels
that may be moved in a courtyard,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another case about broken pieces, this time brought as a ברייתא with a מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, pieces of an old oven may be moved.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: they may not be moved
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees and forbids moving the pieces of an old oven.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: they may not be moved.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives the opposing view in the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that the pieces of the oven are not considered useful items, so they are מוקצה. This forms a clear מחלוקת with רבי מאיר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
They may not be moved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי מאיר in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, pieces of an old oven are מוקצה.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's testimony supporting the lenient view
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי testifies, in the name of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, that pieces of an old oven may be moved on שבת, and that its cover may be moved even without a handle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי testified in the name of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב about pieces of an old oven: they may be moved on שבת. He also testified about the oven's cover: it does not need a handle.
steps.whatsHappening: An older tradition is brought that agrees with רבי מאיר's lenient view. It also adds a second ruling about the oven's cover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The testimony supports רבי מאיר against רבי יהודה. Usually, a lid needs a handle to count as a כלי that may be moved. The oven's cover may be moved even without a handle.
steps.whatToRemember: The pieces of an old oven are a מחלוקת between רבי מאיר (permitted) and רבי יהודה (forbidden). רבי יוסי's testimony supports the lenient view and adds that the oven's cover needs no handle.

phrases.aramaic: הֵעִיד רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei testified in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov
about pieces of an old oven
that they may be moved on Shabbat,
and about its cover,
that it does not need a handle.
phrases.notes: It may be moved even without a handle.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵעִיד רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי מאיר's lenient view from step 7 against רבי יהודה in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pieces of an old oven may be moved, and its cover may be moved even without a handle.

steps.title: What is the argument really about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the root of the argument about oven pieces is.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what idea lies behind the argument between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה about pieces of an old oven. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know who permits and who forbids. Now the גמרא wants the reason behind each side.

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ברייתא argument in steps 7-8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that divides רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה about oven pieces.

steps.title: אביי: it depends on what kind of use the pieces have
steps.stepSummary: אביי says they argue about pieces that have some use, but not a use like their original one.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: They disagree about pieces that can do some kind of job, but not a job like their original job. רבי יהודה follows his own view, and רבי מאיר follows his own view.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that oven pieces can still be used for something, but they can no longer be used as an oven. That is exactly where the two תנאים already argued in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, one view says broken pieces may be moved if they can do any job. רבי יהודה says they must do a job similar to their original job. Oven pieces fit the middle case, so רבי מאיר permits and רבי יהודה forbids.

keyTerms.meaning: Able to do some kind of job
A job similar to their original job
He follows his own reasoning, as stated elsewhere

phrases.english: Abaye said:
About pieces that do some kind of job,
but do not do a job like their original one, they disagree.
And Rabbi Yehuda follows his own reasoning,
and Rabbi Meir follows his own reasoning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The argument depends on whether pieces with some use, but not their original use, may be moved. This matches the argument in the משנה.

steps.title: רבא: then why mention an oven at all?
steps.stepSummary: רבא objects that, by אביי's logic, they should have argued about any broken כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: If so, instead of arguing about oven pieces, let them argue about broken כלים in general!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges אביי's explanation. If the issue is only about pieces that lost their original use, why does the ברייתא choose an oven specifically?
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's principle applies to every broken כלי. Choosing an oven suggests something special about ovens, and אביי's answer does not explain what that is.

phrases.english: Rava strongly objected to this:
If so,
instead of disagreeing about pieces of an oven,
let them disagree about ordinary broken utensils!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's answer in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the argument is just the general dispute about broken pieces.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the principle is general, the ברייתא's choice of an oven is unexplained.

steps.title: רבא: they argue about one particular kind of oven
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a new explanation: the argument is about pieces of a specific type of oven.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: They disagree about the pieces of this particular kind of oven.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא replaces אביי's explanation with his own. He says the ברייתא is about a special oven, and he is about to show which one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows that אביי's approach is dropped. Now the oven really matters, which answers רבא's own question about why the ברייתא mentions an oven.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; this signals that the earlier answer is rejected

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
They disagree about the pieces of this particular oven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's answer after the objection in step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument is about broken utensils in general (אביי).
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is about one specific kind of oven, explained next.

steps.title: The משנה about an oven set over a pit
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a משנה where רבי יהודה and חכמים argue whether an oven set over a pit can become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: If someone placed an oven over the opening of a pit or a cistern and put a stone there, רבי יהודה says: If it is heated from below and becomes hot at the top, it can become טמא. If not, it is טהור. חכמים say: Since it can be heated in some way, it can become טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא shows which oven he means. It is an oven that was not set up the normal way but placed over a pit. רבי יהודה says it counts as a real כלי only if it works well. חכמים say it counts as long as it can be heated at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, a poorly set-up oven is not a real כלי even when it is whole, so its pieces certainly may not be moved. According to חכמים (רבי מאיר), it is a real כלי, so its pieces may be moved like any כלי. This explains why the ברייתא is about an oven.

keyTerms.meaning: Able to become ritually impure / not able to

steps.confusionAlert: Here טמא does not mean the oven is already impure. It means the oven counts as a real כלי that can become impure. טהור means it is not a proper כלי at all.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
If he placed it over the opening of a pit
or over the opening of a cistern
and put a stone there,
Rabbi Yehuda says:
If one heats it from below
and it becomes heated at the top, it can become impure;
and if not, it is pure.
And the Rabbis say:
Since it is heated in any case, it can become impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source and the case for רבא's explanation in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that the oven argument is about a specially set-up oven.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה (כלים) about an oven placed over a pit or cistern.

steps.title: What is the root of the oven-over-a-pit argument?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what lies behind the argument between רבי יהודה and חכמים in that משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And about what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks for the source behind the argument in the משנה it just quoted. This sets up the explanation from a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having brought the משנה, the גמרא wants to know where each side's view comes from.

phrases.english: And about what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the reasoning behind the משנה in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis of the argument between רבי יהודה and חכמים.

steps.title: The argument comes from how they read the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה reads the פסוק as covering only an oven that is whole and working. חכמים read it as covering an oven in any case.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about this פסוק: 'An oven or a stove shall be broken; they are טמא and they shall be טמא to you.' רבי יהודה holds: an oven that still needs to be smashed can become טמא, but one that does not need smashing is טהור. חכמים hold: 'They shall be טמא to you' means in any case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that both sides read the same פסוק differently. רבי יהודה says only a working oven, one that would need to be smashed to remove its impurity, is a real כלי. A weak oven over a pit already counts as broken. חכמים say the extra words 'they shall be טמא to you' include every oven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says a טמא oven must be smashed. רבי יהודה learns that only an oven that 'lacks smashing,' meaning it is whole and working, counts as a כלי. An oven over a pit is treated as already broken. חכמים learn from 'טמאים יהיו לכם' that it counts as a כלי however it was set up.

keyTerms.meaning: Still needs smashing, meaning it is whole and working

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's explanation: the oven pieces argument is about an oven set over a pit. רבי יהודה says even the whole oven was never a real כלי, so its pieces cannot be moved. רבי מאיר (חכמים) says it was a real כלי, so its pieces can be moved.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ties a law about moving things on שבת to a law about טומאה. Whether something can be moved on שבת depends on whether it counts as a real כלי.

phrases.english: About this verse:
"An oven or a stove shall be smashed;
they are impure, and they shall be impure to you,"
Rabbi Yehuda holds:
one that still needs smashing can become impure;
one that does not need smashing is pure.
And the Rabbis hold:
"They shall be impure to you" means in any case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה reads the פסוק as applying only to a working oven. חכמים read 'טמאים יהיו לכם' as including any oven.

steps.title: What do חכמים do with the word יותץ?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why חכמים do not learn from the word "יוּתָּץ" the way רבי יהודה does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for חכמים too, isn't the word "it shall be broken" written in the פסוק?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges חכמים. The word "יוּתָּץ" is in the פסוק, so what do they learn from it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה used "יוּתָּץ" to limit טומאה to a whole, working oven. חכמים say an oven is טמא in any case. So it looks like the word "יוּתָּץ" does nothing for them, and the גמרא asks why.

keyTerms.meaning: "It shall be smashed". This word comes from the פסוק about a טמא oven.
"But isn't it written?" This phrase introduces a verse used as a challenge.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis too,
isn't it written: "it shall be broken"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how חכמים deal with the verse that רבי יהודה used in step 16.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every word in a פסוק should teach something. If חכמים ignore "יוּתָּץ", the word teaches them nothing.

steps.title: חכמים use it the other way: an attached oven is still impure
steps.stepSummary: חכמים use "יוּתָּץ" to teach that an oven attached to the ground is not treated like the ground itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: That word teaches the opposite direction. You might have thought that since he attached it to the ground, it counts as the ground itself. So the פסוק teaches us that it can still become טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that חכמים do use "יוּתָּץ". They use it to make the oven more טמא, not less.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something attached to the ground normally cannot become טמא. You might think an oven over a pit is like the ground. "יוּתָּץ" teaches that it can be smashed and taken out, so it is still a כלי that can become טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Attached to the ground. Such things cannot become טמא.

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides use the same word "יוּתָּץ", but in opposite directions. רבי יהודה uses it to LIMIT טומאה. חכמים use it to INCLUDE an attached oven in טומאה.

phrases.english: That verse is for the other direction,
for it would enter your mind to say:
since he attached it to the ground,
it is like the ground itself,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the verse to a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An oven attached to the ground counts as the ground and cannot become טמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the oven can be smashed and removed, it is still a כלי and can become טמא.

steps.title: What does רבי יהודה do with 'they shall be impure to you'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now asks the same question of רבי יהודה about the words "טמאים יהיו לכם".
steps.simpleTranslation: And for the other side, רבי יהודה, isn't it written: "they shall be impure to you"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the same question around. חכמים learn "in any case" from "טמאים יהיו לכם", so what does רבי יהודה do with those words?
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים read "טמאים יהיו לכם" as including every oven. רבי יהודה limits טומאה to a whole, working oven. So these words seem to teach him nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: "The other one". Here it means רבי יהודה.
"They shall be impure to you". This phrase is from the same פסוק.

phrases.english: And the other one too,
isn't it written: "they shall be impure to you"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 17, now aimed at רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: How רבי יהודה reads the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase seems to have no job in רבי יהודה's reading.

steps.title: שמואל's rule: the argument is only about the first firing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה uses the verse the way שמואל explains: the argument is only about the first firing. After a second firing, the oven is טמא anywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: That phrase follows what רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the argument is about the first firing. But after the second firing, it is טמא even if it hangs on a camel's neck.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהודה uses "טמאים יהיו לכם" for the case of an oven that was fired a second time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A clay oven becomes a finished כלי when it is first fired. רבי יהודה and חכמים argue only about that first firing over a pit. Once the oven has been fired a second time, everyone agrees it is a full כלי and טמא anywhere, even hanging on a camel. That is what "טמאים יהיו לכם" teaches רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: The first firing of a new clay oven, which finishes it as a כלי
A second firing, after the oven is already complete
Hanging on a camel's neck. This means totally unattached and portable.

phrases.english: That verse
is like Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel.
For Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
The dispute is about the first firing,
but regarding the second firing,
it is impure even if it hangs on a camel's neck.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two people here. רב יהודה (the אמורא quoting שמואל) is a different person from רבי יהודה (the תנא in the dispute).
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the dispute to one case and assigns the verse to the case everyone agrees on
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "טמאים יהיו לכם" has no job for רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי יהודה, the phrase teaches that after a second firing the oven is טמא wherever it is.

steps.title: עולא: for חכמים even the first firing makes it impure anywhere
steps.stepSummary: עולא says that according to חכמים, even after the first firing, the oven is טמא even if it hangs on a camel's neck.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: and the first firing, according to חכמים, makes it טמא even if it hangs on a camel's neck.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא adds a ruling to explain the חכמים side of שמואל's split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל only told us that the second firing makes the oven טמא anywhere. עולא says that for חכמים the first firing is already enough, even for a totally portable oven. So the whole argument is really about רבי יהודה's view of the first firing.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sharpens the picture: for רבי יהודה, an oven fired once over a pit is not a כלי at all. רב אשי builds his challenge on exactly that point.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
And the first firing, according to the Rabbis,
makes it impure even if it hangs on a camel's neck.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds to שמואל's rule by giving the חכמים side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to חכמים, the first firing makes the oven טמא even when it is completely detached and portable.

steps.title: רב אשי: why argue about the pieces and not the oven itself?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges רבא: if רבי יהודה does not consider the oven itself a כלי, why would the argument be about its broken pieces?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objected: if so, instead of arguing about the pieces of an oven, let them argue about the oven itself! Now, if according to רבי יהודה the oven itself is not a כלי, do we even need to say that its pieces are not?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks רבא's explanation from step 13, that the argument is about pieces of this kind of oven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that for רבי יהודה, the whole oven (fired once over a pit) is not a כלי. Then it is obvious that its broken pieces are not כלים either. So the argument should have been about the whole oven, the bigger case, and not the pieces.

keyTerms.meaning: "Is it even necessary to say?" This marks something obvious.

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי's challenge uses the rule "why argue about the small case when the big case already covers it?" This weakens רבא's explanation that the argument is about oven pieces.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi objected to this:
If so,
instead of disputing about the pieces of an oven,
let them dispute about the oven itself.
Now, the oven itself,
according to Rabbi Yehuda, is not a vessel;
its pieces, is it even necessary to say?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: אִי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the conclusions of steps 20 and 21 to attack רבא's explanation in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's explanation that the argument is about pieces of an oven placed over a pit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the whole oven is not a כלי for רבי יהודה, then saying its pieces are not כלים is obvious. So the argument should have been stated about the whole oven.

steps.title: רב אשי returns to the original explanation: the shards are used as a baking tile
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the מחלוקת is about shards of any oven that are used as a baking tile (טפקא). רבי מאיר argues using רבי יהודה's own standard.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: It really is as we said at first, and the case is where the shard is used to make a baking tile. רבי מאיר is arguing on רבי יהודה's terms. He says: 'In my view, a shard may be moved even if it does any kind of useful work. But even in your view, at least agree that here it is doing the oven's own kind of work!'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers his own question from Step 22 by offering a new way to understand the מחלוקת. The shards are fit to be used as a baking tile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that a broken piece stays a כלי only if it does work similar to its original job (מעין מלאכתו). רבי מאיר holds that any useful work is enough. Here רבי מאיר argues that even by רבי יהודה's stricter rule, baking on a shard is the oven's own work, so the shard should be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A flat clay baking tile or board
According to me / according to you

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר is not changing his own opinion here. He is only saying: 'Even if I use YOUR rule, I still win in this case.'

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
Actually, it is as we said at first,
phrases.notes: The case is shards of any oven, not only an oven that was never a כלי.

phrases.english: and it is where he uses it to make a baking tile,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר לִדְבָרָיו דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה קָאָמַר:
phrases.english: and Rabbi Meir is speaking according to Rabbi Yehuda's own view:
According to me, it is allowed even when they do any useful work,
but according to you,
at least agree with me
that in a case like this, it is doing its own original work!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: לְעוֹלָם כְּדַאֲמַרַן מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Drops רבא's explanation, which step 22 refuted, and returns to אביי's framing from step 11. It answers רבא's objection from step 12: an oven is mentioned because oven shards can serve as a baking tile.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא): shards used as a baking tile, with רבי מאיר arguing by רבי יהודה's own standard.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא's view: the argument is about an oven set over a pit, which רבי יהודה does not consider a כלי at all. Before that, רבא had objected that אביי's general reading could not explain why an oven is mentioned.
steps.terutzMaskana: The oven is a כלי. The argument is whether a shard used as a baking tile counts as doing 'its own work.'

steps.title: רבי יהודה: a baking tile is not like an oven
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה rejects the comparison. An oven is heated from inside and bakes standing up. A tile is heated from outside and does not stand.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה says: It is not similar. There (the whole oven), it is heated from the inside. Here (the tile), it is heated from the outside. There, it bakes standing upright. Here, it does not stand upright.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה answers רבי מאיר's argument from Step 23. Baking on a shard is not the same kind of work an oven does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה points to two real differences in how the baking works: the location of the heat and the position of the vessel. Because the work is different, it does not count as מעין מלאכתו, so by his rule the shard may not be moved.
steps.whatToRemember: By רב אשי's explanation, everyone agrees an oven is a כלי. They argue only about whether a shard used as a baking tile does work 'like the oven.' רבי יהודה says no, because of how it is heated and how it stands.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda: it is not similar.
There (the oven), its heating is from inside;
here (the tile), its heating is from outside.
There, it bakes standing upright;
here, it does not stand upright.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יהודה rejects רבי מאיר's argument from Step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי מאיר's claim that using a shard as a baking tile counts as the oven's own function.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The comparison ignores two real differences: the heat source (inside versus outside) and the position (standing versus lying flat).

steps.title: Testimony that old oven shards and handle-less covers may be moved
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי testified in the name of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב that shards of an old oven may be moved on שבת, and that an oven cover does not need a handle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי testified in the name of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב about the shards of an old oven, that they may be moved on שבת. He also testified about its cover, that it does not need a handle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes again the testimony from the ברייתא already seen in step 9. This sets up רבינא's practical question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same testimony quoted in step 9, repeated so that רבינא can build on it. On the shards, it agrees with רבי מאיר's lenient view: they may be moved on שבת. It adds that the oven's cover counts as a כלי by itself, even without a handle to hold it.

keyTerms.meaning: Testified (passed on a teaching as testimony)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei testified
in the name of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov
about shards of an old oven
that they may be moved on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל כִּיסּוּיוֹ שֶׁאֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ בֵּית יָד.
phrases.english: and about its cover, that it does not need a handle.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵעִיד רַבִּי יוֹסֵי מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the analysis of the מחלוקת ends, it returns to the last clause of the ברייתא (step 9) so that רבינא can comment on the oven-cover ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Old oven shards may be moved on שבת, and an oven cover may be moved even without a handle.

steps.title: רבינא asks whose view the מתא מחסיא practice follows
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks: whose opinion allows people today to move the oven covers of מתא מחסיא, which have no handles?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: According to whom do we nowadays move the covers of the ovens of מתא מחסיא, which have no handle to hold?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא raises a practical question about a local custom. He sets up his own answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally one might think a cover without a handle is not a proper כלי and so may not be moved. רבינא looks for the source that permits the common practice.

keyTerms.meaning: מתא מחסיא, a town in בבל (Babylonia)
A place to grip; a handle

phrases.english: Ravina said:
According to whom do we nowadays move
the covers of the ovens of the town of Mechasya
which have no handle to hold?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא from Step 25 to a real-life practice.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view allows moving oven covers that have no handles?

steps.title: The practice follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that the practice follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom? According to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers his own question. The custom of moving handle-less covers is based on רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's testimony.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects the ברייתא in Step 25 to actual practice. It shows that people relied on רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's lenient view about oven covers.

keyTerms.meaning: According to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the testimony was put into practice. An oven cover without a handle may be moved on שבת.

phrases.english: According to whom? According to Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's question from Step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The practice in מתא מחסיא follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

steps.title: New משנה: a stone inside a water gourd
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: if a stone placed in a water gourd stays in place while drawing water, one may use the gourd on שבת. If the stone falls out, one may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A stone that is in a gourd used for drawing water: if people draw water with it and the stone does not fall out, one may draw water with it. If not, one may not draw water with it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins on a new case. It deals with a stone used as a weight inside a hollow gourd for drawing water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The stone helps the gourd sink so it fills with water. If the stone is firmly attached, it becomes part of the vessel and is not מוקצה. If it is loose and falls out, it stays a plain stone, so using the gourd would mean moving a מוקצה stone.

keyTerms.meaning: A hollow gourd used to draw water

steps.confusionAlert: The test is not about the stone being heavy or useful. It is about whether the stone is firmly attached, so that it becomes part of the vessel.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A stone that is in a water-drawing gourd,
if they draw water with it and it does not fall out,
one may draw water with it;
and if not, one may not draw water with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה after the discussion of oven shards has ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A stone firmly fixed in a gourd counts as part of the vessel, so the gourd may be used on שבת. A loose stone does not, so the gourd may not be used.
